title: 400 Buildings, One Country's Worth of Emissions
summary: Picture 400 big buildings. Now picture a whole country. According to a new Harvard University report, those 400 buildings — America's largest data centers — pumped out more greenhouse gas in a year than the entire nation of Denmark. Denmark has millions of people, homes, hospitals, and factories. The data centers matched all of that. The study looked at the year from May 2024 to April 2025. In that time, data centers used nearly 2 percent of all the energy in the United States. They also produced more than 25 million metric tons of carbon dioxide — two or three times higher than an earlier estimate from 2018. The study's lead author is Gianluca Guidi, a Harvard researcher focused on artificial intelligence and public health. Guidi says the study is already almost a year old. Since then, the build-out has sped up. Early results from newer studies suggest there are now around 1,000 hyperscale data centers — more than double the number in the report. That means the real emissions could be much higher than the study shows. Along with emissions, Guidi points to water use and possible health effects. Power plants that feed data centers can release pollutants that travel through the air and that people eventually breathe. Four states — Virginia, Iowa, Oregon, and Ohio — account for half of the data centers' electricity use, Guidi said. But Guidi says the benefits of the expansion are not always felt by the same communities that carry the environmental costs. More demand for power can mean more power plants, more pollution, and more pressure on local infrastructure. Those consequences do not stop at the data center's fence, he said. Some argue the build-out is needed to keep the country competitive and support the economy and national security.
why_it_matters: Data centers power the online services people use every day, but their energy use affects the air, water, and climate in the communities around them. How they grow will shape both the technology people rely on and the environment they live in.

background_read: A data center is a large building filled with computers that store information and run online services, from videos to artificial intelligence tools.
Those computers run all day and night, so they need a huge amount of electricity, and the power plants that supply it can release greenhouse gases and other pollution.
Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere, which warms the planet, and the pollution from power plants can also affect the air people breathe.
Because data centers are being built so fast, researchers study how much energy and water they use and who feels the costs and the benefits.
